metadataReview.note: The official development plan of the parish of Victoria del Portete, published in the Registro Oficial, describes the Templete del Portete de Tarqui on the Portete–Tinajillas knot as the memorial raised to those who fought the Battle of Tarqui, inaugurated in 1936 under Sucre's instruction to build an obelisk at the Portete de Tarqui. The parish's official history states that the battle was fought across its plains, hills and ravines. The atlas point is the gazetteer node for the Templete, a battlefield-sector reference beside the El Portete hamlet, not a troop position or the full extent of the fighting. The existing date is retained: both official sources give 27 February 1829, a discrepancy left for a separate date review. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Nominatim lookup of OpenStreetMap node 7017521012 (historic=monument, tagged name 'Templete de la Batalla de Tarqu', truncated in OpenStreetMap, Victoria del Portete / Girón) returns latitude -3.1075632 and longitude -79.1096587, rounded to [-79.1097,-3.1076]. The parish PDOT identifies the Templete as the obelisk ordered by Sucre for the Portete de Tarqui; the El Portete hamlet node lies about 400 m to the north-east. This is a memorial and battlefield-sector reference, not a surveyed position of either army or the centre of the engagement. No positional accuracy radius is claimed.
